concerns.text: FR-002 states the baseline asymptotic formula does **not** directly employ the density metrics π(n), 1/ln(n), or ∑_{p≤n}1/p, yet the provided expression for Q_{as}(n) = C n^{-3/4} exp(2√{n/(2 ln n)}) explicitly contains the term 1/ln n. Because the predictor 1/ln n is baked into the baseline, the log‑residual R(n) = log p_{\mathcal{P}}(n) – log Q_{as}(n) is not independent of that predictor, making the validation circular and guaranteeing a non‑zero coefficient regardless of any genuine systematic bias.

FR-005 allows the analyst to “fit an OLS (or thin‑plate‑spline GAM) regression,” i.e., to choose post‑hoc between a linear model and a flexible GAM. This model‑selection flexibility is not pre‑registered and introduces data‑driven fishing, inflating Type I error and undermining the claim that the analysis will objectively test the hypothesised density‑dependent correction.

FR-004 lists π(n), 1/ln n, and ∑_{p≤n}1/p as independent predictors but acknowledges high VIF (>5) without specifying a concrete mitigation strategy (e.g., variable selection, regularisation, or orthogonalisation). The collinearity between π(n) ≈ n/ln n and 1/ln n violates regression assumptions, rendering coefficient significance tests unreliable.

SC-001 requires a statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05) but the specification provides no power analysis. Autocorrelation in the ordered sequence of n reduces the effective sample size, so the detectable effect size is unknown; without a power calculation the claimed significance threshold may be unattainable or misleading.

The plan does not account for plausible confounding factors such as prime‑gap structure or higher‑order terms from the generating function. Omitting these variables can produce spurious associations between R(n) and the chosen density features, threatening the validity of any inferred systematic correction.
